files.lesson.md: --- order: 11 unit: chance node: AC9M8P02 n1 uses: [AC9M8P01 n1, AC9M7P01 n2] title: Venn diagrams and two-way tables summary: "When everyone in a group is sorted by two yes/no questions, a Venn diagram and a two-way table show the same four groups: one, the other, both and neither. Each person is in exactly one of them." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "In a class of 30, 20 play sport and 13 play music. That adds to 33, more than the class. Nobody miscounted. What is going on?" connection: survey-two-way # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8329 url: http://127.0.0.1:8329/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: venn.yml#explain-pic, caption: "30 students: 12 sport only, 8 both, 5 music only, 5 neither. Music (shaded) is 8 + 5 = 13: the table's Music total." } explainClip: query: { code: "@venn.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Four groups, two pictures" say: "The Venn diagram and the table show the same four groups." clip: - caption: { text: "Music only: 5. In the table, Music and not sport.", say: "Music only is five." } - click: Music only - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Add both: 8. Everyone who plays music is 13, the column total.", say: "Add the eight who do both. Thirteen play music." } - click: Sport and Music - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "13 of 30" } - wait: 1500 --- A **Venn diagram** shows two properties as overlapping circles inside a box (everyone). A **two-way table** shows the same people in rows and columns, with totals. ## Predict: more than the class ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an explanation for 20 + 13 > 30 shows whether they think of people who are in both groups." check: type: predict q: "In a class of 30, 20 play sport and 13 play music. 20 + 13 = 33. How can that be?" options: ["Someone made a mistake", "Some play both, and were counted twice", "Some play neither"] actual: "Some play both. They were counted once with sport and again with music. Here 8 play both." ``` ## Run: find the groups ```step stage: run insight: "Choosing regions shows each person is in exactly one of four groups, and a whole circle is two of them." try: { playground: board, starter: "venn.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Choose everyone who plays sport: click the parts of the diagram (or the table, or the buttons). Does it match the table's total? Who was counted twice in your prediction?", when: "x = 1 and y = 1 and z = 0 and w = 0", explain: "Sport only (12) and both (8) make 20. The 8 who play both are also in the music circle: 20 + 13 counts them twice." } ``` Click a part again to remove it. The table's inside cells match the four parts of the diagram: | | Music | Not music | |---|---|---| | **Sport** | both | sport only | | **Not sport** | music only | neither | ## Investigate: build them from a story ```step stage: investigate insight: "Start with the overlap and subtract it from each circle's total; putting a whole total in the 'only' part counts the overlap twice (Lia)." tasks: - check: type: number q: "40 people: 22 like tea, 18 like coffee and 7 like both. How many like neither?" answer: 7 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["-7", "Tea only is 22 − 7 = 15, not 22."] - ["0", "Tea only is 15 and coffee only is 11. Add the 7 in both and take the total from 40."] explain: "Tea only 22 − 7 = 15, coffee only 18 − 7 = 11. 15 + 7 + 11 = 33, so 40 − 33 = 7 like neither." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#lia" text: "Lia draws the Venn diagram for the same 40 people. Click the line where she goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: venn-double-count explain: "Line 3: 22 like tea, but 7 of them are already in the overlap. Tea only is 15 and coffee only is 11. A negative count shows something went wrong." - check: type: question q: "Which is easier to read from a two-way table than from a Venn diagram?" options: ["Who is in neither", "Nothing: they show different people", "The totals, such as how many play sport in all", "Who is in both groups"] answer: 2 feedback: ["Both show neither.", "They show the same people.", null, "Both show the overlap."] explain: "The table has total rows and columns; in a Venn diagram you add the parts yourself." ``` ### Neither Here is the routine. Start in the middle. ```worked 25 \text{ students: } 15 \text{ dog},\ 10 \text{ cat},\ 4 \text{ both} :: Read the story. \text{both} = 4 :: Write the overlap first. \text{dog only} = 15 - 4 = 11,\ \text{cat only} = 10 - 4 = 6 :: Take the overlap from each total. \text{neither} = 25 - (11 + 4 + 6) = 4 :: Everyone else. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Lia's working. Can a group have −7 people? ### Tables or diagrams ## Modify: from one to the other ```step stage: modify insight: "Filling a table from a diagram and a diagram from a table shows the four cells are the four regions." try: { playground: board, starter: "venn.yml#totable", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "venn.yml#totable" hint: ["Both goes where the Dog row meets the Cat column.", "Dog only goes in the Dog row, Not cat column."] check: { type: board, text: "Fill in the two-way table from the Venn diagram.", when: "k = 1", explain: "Dog and cat 4, dog not cat 9, cat not dog 6, neither 11. The totals check it: 13 have a dog, 10 a cat, 30 in all." } - starter: "venn.yml#tovenn" hint: "The overlap is the cell where Glasses meets Left-handed." check: { type: board, text: "Now fill in the Venn diagram's four numbers from the table.", when: "k = 1", explain: "Glasses only 7, both 2, left-handed only 3, neither 16." } - check: type: number q: "In the Sport and Music class (12 sport only, 8 both, 5 music only, 5 neither), how many students do exactly one of the two?" answer: 17 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["25", "That includes the 8 who do both."] explain: "Sport only and music only: 12 + 5 = 17." - check: type: question q: "Which cell of the two-way table matches the part of the Venn diagram outside both circles?" options: ["Music and not sport", "Not sport and not music", "Sport and music", "The total"] answer: 1 feedback: ["That is the music-only part.", null, "That is the overlap.", "The total is everyone."] explain: "Outside both circles means in neither group." ``` ### Diagram to table ### Table to diagram ### Exactly one ### Outside the circles ## Practise: tables and diagrams ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading and completing tables and diagrams, mixed; the overlap counted twice is the planted slip; complements are the review." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A two-way table: 18 students walk and own a bike, 7 walk and don't own a bike. How many students walk in all?" answer: 25 tolerance: 0 explain: "The Walk row: 18 + 7 = 25." - check: type: number q: "60 people: 35 have a phone case, 20 have a screen protector, 12 have both. How many have a case but no screen protector?" answer: 23 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["35", "12 of the 35 have a screen protector too."] explain: "35 − 12 = 23." - check: type: number q: "In that group of 60, how many have neither?" answer: 17 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["5", "60 − 35 − 20 counts the 12 with both twice."] explain: "Case only 23, both 12, protector only 8: 43. So 60 − 43 = 17 have neither." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Same 60 people: 35 have a case, 20 have a screen protector, 12 have both. How many have a screen protector but no case?", answer: 8, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[20, "12 of those 20 have a case too."]], explain: "20 − 12 = 8 have a protector only. Now put the four groups together." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: a bag has 7 counters, 2 of them green. What is P(not green)?" answer: "5/7" explain: "1 − 2/7 = 5/7." ``` ### Row total ### Case only ### Neither ### Review: complement ## Make: your own survey ```step stage: make insight: "Planning a two-question survey and its table and diagram shows they can set up both representations." try: { playground: board, starter: "venn.yml#make", height: 560 } hint: ["Pick two yes/no questions, such as 'Do you catch a bus?' and 'Do you ride a bike?'", "Count the overlap first."] check: { type: reflect, text: "I chose two yes/no questions, counted the four groups (one, the other, both, neither), and drew both a Venn diagram and a two-way table with totals." } ``` The board shows a finished example (bus and bike) to compare with. Ask your two questions to your class or family, then draw both pictures. Which is quicker to read, and for which question? ## Make: on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Finding 'neither' in a made-up walk-and-sport survey, with the reason for subtracting the overlap picked at the key step." check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A survey of 40 Year 8 students finds 22 walk to school, 15 play a sport and 9 do both (made up). How many do neither? Draw the two circles or a table on paper." steps: - ["Walk only: $22 - 9 = 13$. Sport only: $15 - 9 = 6$", "take the overlap out of each total"] - ["$13 + 6 + 9 = 28$ do at least one", "add the three parts, with the overlap counted once"] - ["$40 - 28 = 12$ do neither", "everyone else"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is the overlap counted only once?" options: ["Students who do both are in both totals, so they must be counted once", "Everyone is in exactly one group, so 22 + 15 is right", "The 9 should be taken from the walkers only"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "22 + 15 = 37 counts the 9 twice.", "The 9 are in both totals, so both groups lose them to the overlap."] answer: "12" answerLabel: "Neither" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["3", "That is 40 − 22 − 15, which takes the 'both' students away twice."] - ["28", "That is how many do at least one. Neither is what is left of the 40."] criteria: - "I wrote the overlap, 9, first." - "I counted the overlap once in the total." - "My four parts add to 40." explain: "13 + 6 + 9 = 28 do at least one, so 40 − 28 = 12 do neither. The four cells add to 40." ``` Do this one in your book or on paper, one step per line, before you type the number. **Also used in** - **School surveys.** Walk or ride? Sport or music? Every student falls in one of four cells. - **Clubs and rosters.** Count members of two clubs without counting the shared ones twice. - **Class work.** Survey your class and check the four cells add to the number surveyed. ```teacher summary: Students read, build and convert between Venn diagrams and two-way tables for two yes/no properties (AC9M8P02, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can sort a group into one, the other, both and neither. - I can build a Venn diagram or a two-way table from a story. - I can change a Venn diagram into a two-way table, and back. struggle: The overlap. Ask students to write the 'both' number first, every time, and take it from each total. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need sample spaces and fractions as probabilities. The one idea: two properties make four groups, and every person is in exactly one. The common mistake is writing a whole total (22 like tea) in the 'only' part, counting the overlap twice (Lia's mistake). The board shows the diagram and the table together; choosing a region highlights the matching cell. In Modify, students fill one from the other (the board ticks when all four are right). Probabilities from these (and, or, not) come in two lessons. Tree diagrams and grids (the other representations in 8P02) are next. running: - "Predict: ask who might have been counted twice." - "Run: ask which two groups make the whole Sport circle." - "Investigate: ask Lia how many like tea but not coffee." - "Modify: ask where 'both' goes in the table." - "Make: ask which picture answers 'how many ride a bike in all?' faster." - "Paper: students draw the circles or table in their books first; the page marks the number and the reason for the overlap, then shows a model. Books out." stuck: - see: A student writes the whole total in the 'only' part. ask: Are some of those people in the overlap too? fix: Write both first; only = total − both. - see: A student forgets the 'neither' group. ask: Is everyone in a circle? fix: The box is everyone; neither = total − the other three. - see: A student mixes up rows and columns in the table. ask: "Read the row name, then the column name: what do both say?" fix: Each inside cell is one row property and one column property. stretch: "Three properties need three circles: how many regions does that make? Try it for sport, music and art." support: A blank Venn diagram and a blank two-way table on one sheet, with 'both' marked in each. leads: > This starts AC9M8P02 node 1. Where it leads: grids and tree diagrams (next lesson), and 'and', 'or' and 'not' probabilities. exit: q: "50 students: 30 study French, 25 study Japanese, 10 study both. How many study neither?" a: "French only 20, Japanese only 15, both 10: 45, so 5 study neither." explain: > Sorting a group by two yes/no properties makes four groups: **one only**, **the other only**, **both** and **neither**. Everyone is in exactly one. A **Venn diagram** shows them as two overlapping circles in a box; a **two-way table** shows them as four cells with totals. Write **both** first, then take it from each total. ```

# region: lia
In a group of 40 people, 22 like tea, 18 like coffee and 7 like both.
Lia writes 7 in the overlap of the Venn diagram.
She writes 22 in the tea-only part and 18 in the coffee-only part.
Neither: 40 − 22 − 18 − 7 = −7.
